thread:
Samir: Acme-eng opening an escalation — p99 for streaming endpoints jumped ~3x yesterday, non-stream total time unchanged. repro attached.
acme-eng: seeing lots of initial-delay before first chunk. TTFB up ~800ms p99, total latency similar to before.
Mira: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro curl or SDK call?
acme-eng: sure: curl -i -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"stream":true,"prompt":"test repeat"}'  # repeated 50x. Logged 1.1s until first byte.
Ben: quick check — did you recently switch clients or network path? Any proxy in front?
acme-eng: no change on our side. We did upgrade to SDK v2.3.1 last week but also saw same with raw curl.
Jules: ops-bot can you pull ingress & edge proxy metrics for requests from Acme IPs for the window 2025-11-10 03:00-07:00 UTC?
ops-bot: pulled logs. Edge coalesce flush count spiked at 03:12 UTC, avg flush delay increased from 12ms -> 190ms for streaming connections.
Mira: interesting. Edge coalescing heuristic change was rolled 03:10 UTC to reduce small-payload flushes. Could be correlated.
Samir: acme-eng, can you run a quick comparison: streaming call vs non-streaming call from same host and post timings? e.g.
acme-eng: did that: STREAMING first byte 920ms, total 1.05s. NON-STREAMing total 1.02s. So server is generating fast but first-chunk delay is the issue.
Ben: good repro. Likely path: edge coalescer + client-side TCP buffering (Nagle) + SDK chunking mismatch. Let's try toggles.
Mira: ops-bot, roll a canary that disables the new coalescing heuristic for the region serving Acme.
ops-bot: canary rollout started to 2% of edge hosts at 03:35 UTC.
acme-eng: retested — TTFB dropped to 110ms on canaryed host. Non-canary still 900ms.
Jules: confirm causal link. Proposed mitigation: rollback heuristic or add a short explicit flush window for streaming responses when downstream is likely to be interactive.
Samir: short-term: expand canary to 40% and add header to allow customers to opt-out: X-Redwood-Prefer-Immediate-Flush: true. Long-term: add server-side chunk preflight to force a tiny initial flush when stream=true.
Ben: also push SDK patch to set socket TCP_NODELAY in our Node client and add guidance for fetch keepalive/streaming usage. That will address client-side Nagle interactions.
Mira: creating ops ticket for permanent rollback if metrics don't stabilize. Jules — can you capture p95/p99 dashboards for edge flush delay and overall TTFB for next 2h?
Jules: on it. I've linked dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/edge/flush-delay?org=redwood&from=now-2h
acme-eng: thanks — with canary rolled to 40% our p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 150ms. Appreciate the quick response :clap:
Samir: thanks team. Action items:
- ops: complete gradual rollback OR wire opt-out header (short-term). (Mira)
- eng-runtime: implement forced initial flush for stream=true and add test. (Ben)
- devex: SDK patch for TCP_NODELAY and sample code for immediate-flush header. (Jules)
- support: communicate mitigation and expected timeline to Acme. (Samir)
Ben: I'll open PR for runtime change + unit tests. Targeting patch release in 48h.
Mira: will monitor canary and page if regressions reappear. :eyes:
acme-eng: will validate across their EU cluster tomorrow and report. Thanks again.
Samir: closing loop after dashboard confirms stable p99 for 4h. If any new findings paste here.
